name: Hananiah
overview: Hananiah was a male figure chosen to serve in the court of King Nebuchadnezzar alongside Daniel, as recorded in Daniel 1:6. His selection for this role highlights his significance within the Babylonian captivity context. No tribal affiliation or additional personal notes are provided.
namesAndTitles: The name Hananiah means 'YHWH is gracious,' reflecting a recognition of God's kindness. Additionally, he is known by the name Shadrach, which means 'servant of Aku.' Both names appear in Daniel 1:6-7 and illustrate the dual identity given to him in Babylonian service.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Hananiah beyond his association with Daniel and others chosen for Nebuchadnezzar's service. There are no listed relatives or further relational details.
scriptureSignificance: Hananiah's importance lies in his role as one of the young men taken into Babylonian captivity and selected for royal service, demonstrating God's providence in preserving faithful servants during exile. His presence alongside Daniel marks him as part of the faithful remnant who maintained their devotion to God in a foreign land. This sets the stage for God's miraculous interventions and the testimony of His sovereignty amid adversity.
